summary:
The Northern Mariana Islands is a US commonwealth and stands under the national framework of the United States for travel documents, immigration and airport screening. United States passports and entry documents reflect sex assigned at birth, and the X marker option was eliminated by the January 2025 executive order, so a trans visitor travelling on United States documents presents a gender marker that may not match presentation at the port of entry.

Screening at the airport follows federal procedure, and the order halting federal funding for gender-affirming care reaches federally funded institutions in the territory, so access to such care during a visit cannot be assumed. In February 2025 the United States State Department additionally announced visa denials for trans athletes seeking entry to compete in women's sports.

Consensual same-sex conduct is not criminalised, and same-sex marriage has been legal since 2015 under Obergefell v. Hodges; the first same-sex marriage on Saipan was officiated on 27 July 2015. Adoption has been available since 2015. Legal gender change is permitted provided the applicant has undergone the specified medical process.

Commonwealth-level protections remain limited. CNMI Public Law 22-32, signed in January 2023, amends the Commonwealth Code to provide criteria for enhanced sentencing in hate-motivated crimes, and this hate-crimes statute covers sexual orientation and gender identity. Beyond federal law, discrimination protections extend to government employees only, with no comprehensive commonwealth nondiscrimination coverage beyond federal EEOC recourse.

As of 27 September 2026 the MAP Equality Profile scores the territory's Sexual Orientation Policy Score at 3.5/22 (Low) and Gender Identity Policy Score at -2/25 (Negative), for an overall 1.5/47 (Low), with marriage recognition at 1/1 since 2015.
tangentialFactors:
The territory's negative gender-identity policy score reflects the absence of commonwealth-level protections covering gender identity outside the hate-crimes statute and federal recourse, so a trans visitor should not expect local legal remedies for discrimination in housing, public accommodations or services.

The hate-crimes enhanced-sentencing provision is a protection mechanism rather than a nondiscrimination mandate; it operates after a bias-motivated offence has occurred and does not itself prohibit discriminatory conduct.

The first Gay Pride event in the commonwealth was held at the GIG Discotheque in Garapan with about 60 people attending, and organiser Sharmaine Casquero called it a success, indicating a small but visible public community presence on Saipan.
localsOnly:
Residents of the Northern Mariana Islands may change their legal gender provided they have undergone the specified medical process, and same-sex couples have been able to adopt since 2015.

Discrimination protections at the commonwealth level extend to government employees only, beyond federal law; there is no comprehensive commonwealth nondiscrimination statute covering sexual orientation or gender identity in employment, housing or public accommodations, leaving federal EEOC recourse as the main avenue.

CNMI Public Law 22-32, signed in January 2023, amends the Commonwealth Code to provide criteria for enhanced sentencing of defendants convicted of hate-motivated crimes, with the statute covering sexual orientation and gender identity.
outOfScopeNotes:
The scope of the medical process required for legal gender change in the Northern Mariana Islands, including whether it applies to residents only or also to persons holding commonwealth-issued documents, is not specified in the available sources and remains unresolved.

Whether the January 2025 federal executive order eliminating the X gender marker applies retroactively to previously issued United States passports held by residents of the territory is not sourced here and remains unresolved.

Practical enforcement of the hate-crimes enhanced-sentencing provision in bias-motivated offences against trans persons in the territory is not documented in the available sources and remains unresolved.
